concepts.concept: Per-index lock state (the 32-bit lock_q vector) held across cycles
concepts.writers: Reset: lock_q(i) <= '0' at line 42 when rstn_i = '0'. Update: lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw at line 45 on rising_edge(clk_i), guarded by (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') and (sel(i) = '1') (lines 44-45, in the per-index spinlock process).
concepts.observers: bus_rsp_o.data exposes lock_q: masked read bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel at line 68 (when addr(7) = '0' and read branch active) and full-vector read bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q at line 70 (when addr(7) = '1' and read branch active); bus_rsp_o is an output port (line 23).

confidentiality.reason: The RTL drives the full lock_q vector to the output at line 70 (bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q) on a read request, so an external observer can learn the lock state.

integrity.reason: Each lock bit is written from the external bus at line 45 (lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw) under the bus request guard, so an external writer can change stored lock state.

availability.reason: Writes to lock_q occur only when the write condition on line 44 holds ((bus_req_i.stb='1') and address decode and sel), so external bus signals can freeze or force lock updates and affect availability.

undermined behavior.reason: lock_q is driven only by the internal spinlock process assignment (line 45) with no alternate debug/test override path in the RTL.

concepts.concept: Selected lock index (the one-hot sel vector computed from bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2)) used to pick which lock bit an access targets
concepts.writers: sel(i) is computed combinationally at line 51: sel(i) <= '1' when (bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) = std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(i, 5))) else '0' (driven from bus_req_i.addr).
concepts.observers: sel is not an output itself but is observable via outputs: bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel at line 68 (masked read reveals which sel bit is set); sel is also tested in the write enable condition at line 44.

confidentiality.reason: The masked read at line 68 (bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel) exposes the one-hot sel pattern to an external observer, revealing which index was selected.

integrity.reason: sel is computed directly from the external address at line 51 and is sampled in the write guard at line 44, so changes to bus_req_i.addr can alter sel while a write occurs.

availability.reason: sel is derived from the external bus address (line 51), so control of bus_req_i.addr can hold or change selection and thereby affect whether particular accesses proceed.

undermined behavior.reason: sel has a single combinational driver at line 51 and there is no alternate debug/test override in the RTL.

concepts.concept: Bus request handshake (request strobe and response ACK)  the start event of an access and the ACK the module delivers
concepts.writers: Request strobe is an external input (bus_req_i.stb, port declared at line 22). The module drives ACK at line 63: bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb (and on reset bus_rsp_o is assigned rsp_terminate_c at line 61).
concepts.observers: bus_rsp_o.ack is an output port (declared line 23) and is driven at line 63, so the ACK is observable outside the module.

confidentiality.reason: The module echoes the requester-controlled strobe to ACK at line 63 (bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb), which is a read-back to the requester and does not reveal new secret information.

integrity.reason: ACK is driven from the external strobe (copied at line 63) and the strobe qualifies operations, so an external agent controlling bus_req_i.stb can change the handshake behavior.

availability.reason: The module's ACK and gated operations depend on the external strobe (ack <= bus_req_i.stb at line 63), so control of stb from outside can block or force progress.

undermined behavior.reason: bus_rsp_o.ack has a single internal assignment copying the strobe (line 63) and there is no alternate override or debug path in the RTL.

concepts.concept: Bus operation type (the rw bit)  the request's read/write indicator that determines the stored lock value and read behavior
concepts.writers: bus_req_i.rw is an external input port (declared at line 22); it is consumed internally at line 45 to form stored values (lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw) and at line 66 to select the read branch (if bus_req_i.stb = '1' and bus_req_i.rw = '0' then ...).
concepts.observers: The rw bit affects outputs: the response data path is enabled only for reads (guard at line 66), so bus_rsp_o.data (lines 68/70) and the presence/absence of returned data can reveal rw to observers of the output port bus_rsp_o.

confidentiality.reason: rw is a requester-supplied operation bit and the module only returns data on read requests (guard at line 66), so the requester already knows rw and the RTL does not keep it secret.

integrity.reason: The external rw bit is used to compute and write lock_q at line 45 (lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw), so an external writer can change operation type and thereby affect stored state.

availability.reason: The response data path is gated by the rw bit (the read branch test at line 66), so external control of rw can enable or disable returned data and affect progress.

undermined behavior.reason: rw is provided only via the external bus port (declaration at line 22) and there is no internal override or alternate assignment in the RTL.
